_comment: Latvian month names are international loans (janvāris, februāris) and NOT the Slavic set — that is one quick test that a pack is not Polish or Croatian. The decisive field is monthsInDate: a Latvian date puts the month in the LOCATIVE case, not the genitive that Slavic languages use. 2026. gada 15. augustā is correct; 15. augusts is not, and 15. augusta is the genitive a Slavic-trained writer would reach for and is also wrong. Latvian has seven cases and the locative is one of them. Note the -ī endings (janvārī, septembrī, oktobrī, novembrī, decembrī) against the -ā ones (martā, maijā, augustā): they follow the noun's declension class, not the calendar. The year carries a trailing full stop because it too is an ordinal — 2026. gada, 'of the 2026th year'. Weekdays are numbered words: pirmdiena is literally 'first-day', and svētdiena, 'holy-day', is the only one that is not a number.
